page: Microsoft Azure E8s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz and includes a 50 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a 131 GB SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate memory performance and lower-tier compute capabilities. The instance achieved average ratings in Passmark CPU tests, Passmark memory scores, and Passmark database operations. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes fell within the average range. However, raw CPU performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, and Redis SET operations scoring in the bottom 25%. LLM inference with a small 135M model achieved average text generation speeds but weak prompt processing speeds, while a medium 7B model resulted in poor text generation performance.

Given its high memory density relative to compute resources, the E8s_v3 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require substantial memory capacity without demanding high-frequency CPU performance. It is suited for relational database management systems, caching layers, and enterprise applications with moderate transaction volumes. The inclusion of a local SSD and Premium Storage capability supports workloads requiring reliable disk I/O, though intensive computational tasks or large-scale LLM deployments may face bottlenecks due to the lower-tier CPU performance.
description: Microsoft Azure E8s_v3 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine from the ESv3 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 64.0 GB of RAM, and a 131 GB local SSD. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance is Premium Storage capable. Benchmark data shows average performance in memory bandwidth, Passmark database operations, and software compilation, contrasted with weaker results in raw CPU compute and static web serving. With a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, the E8s_v3 is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance compute. It is best suited for relational databases, caching systems, and moderate enterprise applications.
